Can this reward be trusted?

RL environment · 30 tasks in 3 families · every reward is code · generated Nov 20, 2026, 1:05 AM

Synthetic tasks, scripted agents. The tasks are generated, and the agents are short Python scripts, not language models. The page shows what the task gate catches and how the rewards behave, not model performance.

The tasks

Support tickets · 10 tasks

The agent resolves a damaged-item ticket with six tools: get_policy, get_customer, list_orders, issue_refund, escalate and reply.

Reward pays only for

The right refund for the right amount, or a reply, or an escalation, and nothing else.

Data QC · 10 tasks

The agent queries a payments table in read-only SQLite and flags every row that breaks a rule in the spec.

Reward pays only for

The flagged rows match the bad rows exactly.

Help center retrieval · 10 tasks

The agent searches help center pages, reads one, and answers with the page id, the value and a 5 to 40 word quote copied from that page.

Reward pays only for

Right page, right value, and a quote that is really on the page and contains the value.

Task QC gate

The gate runs before any agent is scored. It plays a reference solution, an agent that does nothing, and seven shortcut agents on every task, then checks the tasks themselves. Three bad tasks were planted in the second set to show what it catches.

Caught by the gate

Answer leaked in the prompt

Task retrieval-dirty-leak. The answer, 90 days, is written into the question, so an agent can copy it without reading a single page.

Customer question: Is the dispute window for business credit cards 90 days? Find the help center page that answers it, then call answer with the doc_id, the value, and a quote of 5 to 40 words copied from that page.

Reward too lenient

Task dataqc-dirty-lenient. Only 4 rows break a rule (rows 15, 20, 21, 22). The reward only checked that those rows were somewhere in the flagged list, so the flag_all shortcut flagged all 24 rows and was paid for it.

Lenient rewardFlagging every row passes.
Exact rewardThe flagged rows must equal the bad rows.

Duplicated task

Tasks tickets-01 and tickets-dirty-dup share the same data, and their prompts overlap 83% by 3-word phrases. Counting both gives one case double weight in every pass rate.

Support ticket from customer C-104: "My espresso machine showed up with a cracked water tank. I want my money back." Resolve it using the tools and the refund policy.
Support ticket from customer C-104: "My espresso machine showed up with a cracked water tank. I want my money back, thanks." Resolve it using the tools and the refund policy.

Shortcut agents on the clean set

A reward that pays a shortcut is a reward an RL run will learn to game.

Shortcut agentWhat it doesTasks passed
nullDoes nothing and submits0/30
always_escalateEscalates every ticket3/10
reply_onlySends a polite reply and never acts3/10
refund_all_ordersRefunds every order the customer has0/10
flag_allFlags every row in the table0/10
flag_last_rowsFlags the last three rows0/10
whole_doc_quoteQuotes the entire page as evidence0/10
echo_questionAnswers with the question itself0/10

The 6 shortcut passes all give the reference answer: escalating is the right call on 3 tickets, and replying is right on 3 others. None is a wrong answer that got paid.

Trace of v2 on tickets-03 (reward 0). The rice cooker was delivered 30 days ago, and the policy refunds damage reported within 30 days. v2 compares with "under 30" instead of "30 or fewer", so it refuses a refund the policy allows. v1 refunded and passed.

1. get_policy {} -> "Refund the full order amount when an item arrives damaged and the customer reports it within 30 days of deliv
2. get_customer {"customer_id": "C-131"} -> {"customer_id": "C-131", "account_flags": []}
3. list_orders {"customer_id": "C-131"} -> [{"order_id": "O-5917", "item": "rice cooker", "amount": 312.99, "days_since_delivery": 30}, {"order_id": "O-5
4. reply {"message": "This order is outside the refund window."} -> "reply sent"
5. submit {} -> "submitted"

Try it

It needs Python 3.10 or newer and nothing else.

git clone https://github.com/priyanka-0207/eval-qc-harness
cd eval-qc-harness
python -m harness env
python -m harness env --dirty --ci

--ci exits 1 when the task gate fails, so a bad task set can block a merge. Per-step traces for every agent are written to reports/env/traces.
